laws.rule: Contamines-Montjoie national nature reserve (Haute-Savoie, near Mont Blanc): from 15 June to 15 September, bivouac (sleeping out, with or without a tent) is prohibited in the zones marked red on the order's map, which cover everything below 2,500 metres and sensitive areas. It is tolerated from 19:00 to 09:00 on two marked sites (Pont de la Rollaz, 40 tents; La Balme, 50 tents) and outside the red zones. Arrêté DDT-2026-0474 of the Haute-Savoie prefect, valid to 31 December 2026.
laws.heading: Arrêté DDT-2026-0474, art 1

laws.rule: In the same reserve, swimming and boating on the lakes and ponds are prohibited all year, including pets swimming, dogs in particular. Arrêté DDT-2026-0474, art 2; the prefect can grant exemptions for research or other justified reasons.
laws.heading: Arrêté DDT-2026-0474, art 2

laws.rule: Écrins National Park (Hautes-Alpes and Isère): camping is prohibited in the core of the park. Bivouac (one night in a small tent you can't stand up in) is allowed only from 19:00 to 09:00 and at least one hour's walk from a road access or from the edge of the core, which is marked by small blue-white-red flags. No fires (a small hiking stove is tolerated), no loud sound from speakers or radios, and all rubbish must be taken out. Bivouac at the Muzelle and Lauvitel lakes is allowed only inside set areas.
laws.heading: Parc national des Écrins, Bivouac

laws.rule: Écrins National Park core: dogs are banned, even on a lead or carried (article 3 of decree 2009-448). Exceptions are working herd dogs, guide dogs and avalanche search dogs. Dogs on a lead are allowed only at a short list of car parks and tracks named by the park (for example Gioberney, Pré de Madame Carle, Dormillouse and Confolens-le-Bas).
laws.heading: Parc national des Écrins, Animaux domestiques

laws.rule: Écrins National Park core: flying any motorised aircraft below 1,000 metres above the ground is prohibited unless the park director authorises it. The park states that drones of any size count as motorised aircraft, so a recreational drone flight over the core is covered by the ban. Paragliding and hang gliding over the core are limited by a director's order to 1 July to 31 October, with limited take-offs from 1 May to 30 June.
laws.heading: Parc national des Écrins, Survols motorisés and non motorisés

laws.rule: Écrins National Park core: picking plants and taking fossils or minerals is prohibited in general. Wild berries listed by the park (such as bilberries, wild strawberries and raspberries) may be picked for family use up to 1 kg per person per day, and combs or other collecting tools are banned. Motor vehicles are banned in the core, including on forest and pastoral tracks, except on named roads and to named car parks.
laws.heading: Parc national des Écrins, Cueillettes et prélèvements; Circulation motorisée

laws.rule: Vanoise National Park core (Savoie): bivouac is allowed in summer only right next to certain staffed refuges, while the refuge is staffed, and a place must be booked in advance with the refuge warden because places are limited. Do not light fires. The park says breaking the bivouac rules can lead to a fine.
laws.heading: Parc national de la Vanoise, Le bivouac en Vanoise; La réglementation dans le cœur du Parc

laws.rule: Vanoise National Park core: dogs are banned, even small, friendly or well-trained ones. The exceptions are herd-protection and herding dogs and dogs that accompany people with a disability.
laws.heading: Parc national de la Vanoise, La réglementation dans le cœur du Parc

laws.rule: Vanoise National Park core: drones count as motorised aircraft and fall under the general ban on flying below 1,000 metres above the ground, unless the park director authorises it (for example scientific work). The park also says not to use airborne objects or craft for sport or leisure in the core. Professional or commercial filming and sound recording in the core is banned by the park's decree except by director's exemption; amateur filming is allowed.
laws.heading: Parc national de la Vanoise, Survol et drone; Prises de vue

laws.rule: Vanoise National Park core: don't pick flowers or fruit, or take insects or minerals. Motor vehicles are banned except on certain tracks where named permits can be issued. Sports events held wholly or partly in the core need prior authorisation from the park.
laws.heading: Parc national de la Vanoise, La réglementation dans le cœur du Parc

laws.rule: Mont Blanc normal route (Goûter route, Haute-Savoie): the French mountain club federation's refuge portal says a ministerial decree prohibits all forms of camping, bivouac included, across the whole Mont-Blanc classified site. The same portal says a prefectural order of 15 June 2020 sets the rules for booking the Nid d'Aigle, Tête-Rousse and Goûter refuges. The order text was a scanned image and could not be read for this record, so check the prefecture's current order before a climb.
laws.heading: FFCAM, Voie normale du Mont Blanc, Public booking information

layers.authority: Parc national de la Vanoise (refuge wardens)
layers.process: Bivouac in the park core is allowed in summer only beside certain staffed refuges, and a place has to be reserved with the refuge warden; numbers per refuge are limited.

layers.authority: Parc national des Écrins / Parc national de la Vanoise
layers.process: Flying a drone below 1,000 m above the ground in either park core needs the park director's authorisation (applied for on the park's online form); recreational flights are otherwise banned. Professional or commercial filming in the Vanoise core needs a director's exemption.

layers.authority: Préfecture de la Haute-Savoie (order of 15 June 2020, as published by FFCAM) and the FFCAM refuge portal
layers.process: Booking for the Nid d'Aigle, Tête-Rousse and Goûter refuges runs through one portal under a prefectural order. All people in the party are named, each non-professional participant uploads a valid identity document (identity card, passport or driving licence), and the booking confirmation must be carried and shown at checks and on arrival at the refuge. Online pre-booking covers up to 12 people; a virtual waiting room can open when pre-booking starts; the FFCAM operator confirms the pre-booking and you have 48 hours to finish it. Fees stated by FFCAM: deposit and booking fee of EUR 5 per booking basket, and administrative fees of EUR 15 per person per night kept if a booking is cancelled for non-compliant details (EUR 15 is about A$23.84 and EUR 5 about A$7.95 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293). Booking for the 2027 season was not open on 7 November 2026. Confirm in writing with the prefecture before relying on the current text.
